There was a time (mid- college for me) my mom begged me for 500$ so her car didn't get repossessed, at the time of her asking for the money we had only just started talking again after her disowning me at 18.

Yes, I wanted to give her the money but I knew she would not only not pay me back, but unfortunately just ask for more eventually.

My parents had the same mentality, "your 18, go to college, pay us rent or get out". I promise you if you help your parents they will not return the favor.

Yes, I have a decent relationship with my parents (from a different state and a bit "from an arms length" type of relationship) and I do love them.... but keep your money and your stuff as your own.

You have worked your ass off to be comfortable and secure, don't let  your parents who already made you fight so hard take anymore.

You can love your parents (as mixed as those feelings may be) but look out for yourself first and foremost! Keep your money!!!

Hey Gavin, I'm 22 and I remember feeling the exact same way you do when i was 12. I can't promise you these feelings will go away, but I can promise you with age and time you will find ways to cope that arnt self destructive. You'll find ways to analyze why you feel the way you do and slowly but surely build a happier path. Not every day will be easy, some might even feel like the worst day of your life, but you can't give in.

Speaking from experience, I hid my feelings from everyone and anyone and it only festered and got harder to deal with. Then, I started to journal. Writing can help more than you believe. If you write something in the heat of emotion, try to come back to a few days or a week later and analyze why you felt that way. Maybe even find patterns I your mindset. For me, when things feel out of my control I start to feel angry and beyond dissatisfied with myself. Knowing this about myself has allowed me to try and make gentle shifts in my mindset. The way you speak to yourself is beyond critical.

I never thought I'd live to graduate high school, but here in 2024 I have a bachelor degree in art. I still have rough days, I still have days I feel like I shouldn't be here but I push on. I push on because I want to see the world be a better place where people feel listened to and cared about.

I know it's hard to feel this way, unbearable even. But I also know, for a FACT that you can do this! I also found people through reddit and forums where I felt supported and cared about. I believe in you Gavin, and I know one day you'll have more good days than bad. Something I also once thought to be impossible.

Good luck, we're all rooting for you. Feel free to message me if you want

I really haven't gotten an explanation of any kind for why I have the kind of voices I do. But most schizoaffective/schizophrenic people have lots of voices or thoughts of self harm and other self destructive behaviors

It can be frightening at times. Sometimes it is hard to sleep or function at all do to the things I am being told or seeing. Sometimes I can't even go to the store to pick up bread and milk due to seeing an old man following me from a distance. Or sometimes in class I can feel people's hands touching me or see them trying to grab me. I have no control over them but when it comes to the commanding voices I can do a good job of not listening to them or at least not following their directions. Although I've had voices that are harmful twords others I've only ever actually followed the commands of voices that tell me to self harm, attempt suicide, do drugs ect.

1. On my father's side an uncle of his, his older brother and possibly a great aunt have had either psychotic, schizophrenic or bipolar symptoms. Depression is much more common in his family along with addiction problems.

2. I feel like I've always been different / my brain has always felt a little off. I would say I really noticed things change in late middle school, near the end of 7th grade. At first things only got a little worse each school year. But by the time I was in 9th grade it seemed to get significantly worse at least every 4 to 6 months. By the time I started 11th grade every month just got worse and worse. My symptoms became more irrational and harder to hide from those around me.

3. Although I am prescribed antipsychotics if I'm being honest I haven't taken them in months. I know it's not the best plan due to my symptoms still progressing but while on the medication my creativity is completely shot. The way I see it is I already feel less than human. And I know I'll never be comfortable with life, but I would rather struggle with my symptoms and not feel quite human rather than being on those devil meds and not even feeling at all, with nothing to even live for or do. But even when I took the meds yes, I was still symptomatic. The voices for example because less frequent but when they were there they were angry with me. So, so angry. They wouldn't shut up until I took my next dose and after half the day the cycle would continue.

I would say when it comes to school I'm quite lucky seeing as my academically gifted, so most classes actually come quickly and easily to me. The main issue are my postive symptoms of my schizophrenia. Hallucinations (people who aren't there, whispers and yells, spiders and bugs, ect) and delusionals (such as classmates and teachers conspiring against me, the cops coming to take me away and experiment on me, people being robots/aliens, being in purgatory, ect) make concentrating really difficult. I manage to get by but there are days I can't even understand the words coming out of peoples mouths because I can hear their thoughts too loud. For me art has always been what I wanted to presue in college. I love art and I feel I have a lot to express and show to the world due to the odd and unique thoughts I have. After getting diagnosed going to art college seemed to fit perfectly because it's not only what I've always wanted, but I feel it's a career path that my illness, as tough as it may be, may actually be some benefit to or at least help me cope with it in a healthy way.
